question: At which of the following places was the inscription of Pratihara king Nagabhata found?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Gwalior, Madhya Pradesh.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Gwalior inscription (Gwalior Prashasti) of the Pratihara ruler Mihira Bhoja records the genealogy and achievements of the Gurjara-Pratihara dynasty, including king Nagabhata (नागभट्ट).

• It celebrates Nagabhata I, who repulsed the Arab invasions, and Nagabhata II, who made Kannauj the Pratihara capital.

• The inscription is a key epigraphic source for the history of the Gurjara-Pratihara dynasty (गुर्जर-प्रतिहार वंश).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The Gurjara-Pratiharas were prominent players in the tripartite struggle for Kannauj against the Palas and the Rashtrakutas.

• Mihira Bhoja (also called Bhoja I) was one of the greatest Pratihara rulers and a devotee of Vishnu, using the title 'Adivaraha'.

NOTE

• Amaravati, Andhra Pradesh (Option 1): An ancient Buddhist site famous for its Amaravati Stupa and school of art, associated with the Satavahanas.

• Agra, Uttar Pradesh (Option 3): A Mughal-era city famous for the Taj Mahal, Agra Fort and Fatehpur Sikri; not linked to Pratihara inscriptions.

• Kandahar, Afghanistan (Option 4): Site of a bilingual (Greek-Aramaic) rock edict of Ashoka, not of the Pratiharas.

question: The Regional Anti-Terrorist Structure body is associated with which of the following International Organisation?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Shanghai Cooperation Organisation.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Regional Anti-Terrorist Structure (RATS) is a permanent organ of the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (शंघाई सहयोग संगठन) headquartered in Tashkent, Uzbekistan.

• RATS coordinates member states' efforts against terrorism, separatism and extremism — the 'three evils'.

• The SCO was founded in 2001 and India became a full member in 2017.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The SCO's founding members were China, Russia, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan and Uzbekistan.

• Its headquarters (Secretariat) is in Beijing, China, while RATS is based in Tashkent.

NOTE

• BRICS (Option 1): A grouping of Brazil, Russia, India, China, South Africa and newer members focused on economic cooperation; has no RATS body.

• Organisation of Islamic Cooperation (Option 3): A body of Muslim-majority nations headquartered in Jeddah; unrelated to RATS.

• SAARC (Option 4): The South Asian Association for Regional Cooperation, headquartered in Kathmandu; it has a Terrorist Offences Monitoring Desk, not RATS.

question: As of 31st July 2025, which of the following is the official language of the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Chinese.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (शंघाई सहयोग संगठन) has two official working languages — Russian and Chinese (चीनी).

• All official SCO documents and proceedings are issued in these two languages.

• The choice reflects the founding role of Russia and China in the organisation.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The SCO covers a large share of the world's population and land area across Eurasia.

• India, along with Pakistan (2017) and Iran (2023), later joined as full members.

NOTE

• Persian (Option 1): The official language of Iran; although Iran is now an SCO member, Persian is not an official SCO language.

• French (Option 3): A UN official language, but not used by the SCO.

• Spanish (Option 4): A widely spoken UN official language, but not an SCO working language.

question: Who was honoured with the Dadasaheb Phalke Lifetime Achievement Award for the year 2022?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Mithun Chakraborty.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Veteran actor Mithun Chakraborty (मिथुन चक्रवर्ती) was conferred the Dadasaheb Phalke Lifetime Achievement Award for 2022, announced in 2024.

• The award recognises his outstanding lifelong contribution to Indian cinema across Hindi, Bengali and regional films.

• Mithun Chakraborty is a National Film Award (राष्ट्रीय फिल्म पुरस्कार) winning actor known for films like 'Mrigayaa' and 'Disco Dancer'.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• He was also honoured with the Padma Bhushan in 2024.

• His debut film 'Mrigayaa' (1976) won him his first National Film Award for Best Actor.

NOTE

• Nagarjuna (Option 1): A leading Telugu film actor and producer; not the 2022 awardee.

• Paresh Rawal (Option 2): A veteran actor and former MP, known for comedy and character roles; not the recipient.

• Salman Khan (Option 3): A popular Bollywood superstar; he was not honoured with this award for 2022.

question: In October 2024, Nayab Singh Saini was elected as the Chief Minister of which state?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Haryana.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Nayab Singh Saini was sworn in as the Chief Minister of Haryana (हरियाणा) in October 2024 after the BJP's victory in the Assembly elections.

• He belongs to the Bharatiya Janata Party (भारतीय जनता पार्टी) and had earlier become CM in March 2024.

• Haryana's capital is Chandigarh, which it shares with Punjab.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• He succeeded Manohar Lal Khattar, who moved to national politics.

• Nayab Singh Saini previously served as a Member of Parliament from Kurukshetra.

NOTE

• Meghalaya (Option 1): A north-eastern state whose Chief Minister is Conrad Sangma; capital Shillong.

• Karnataka (Option 2): A southern state led by CM Siddaramaiah; capital Bengaluru.

• Andhra Pradesh (Option 4): A southern state whose CM (from 2024) is N. Chandrababu Naidu; capital Amaravati.

question: In October 2024, who has been appointed as ambassador of India to France?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Sanjeev Kumar Singla.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Senior IFS officer Sanjeev Kumar Singla was appointed as India's Ambassador to France (फ्रांस में भारत के राजदूत) in 2024.

• He earlier served as India's Ambassador to Israel and as Private Secretary to the Prime Minister.

• The appointment strengthens the India–France strategic partnership (सामरिक साझेदारी).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Singla is a 1997-batch Indian Foreign Service officer.

• India and France cooperate closely in defence, nuclear energy and space.

NOTE

• Hari Babu Kambhampati (Option 1): A BJP politician who has served as Governor (Mizoram/Odisha), not a diplomat to France.

• Rajendra Vishwanath Arlekar (Option 3): A politician who has served as a Governor (Himachal Pradesh, Bihar, Kerala).

• Sandip Goenka (Option 4): Not associated with the ambassadorial appointment to France.

question: In March 2025, which High court division bench comprising Justice C S Sudha questioned the extent to which the state can interfere in regulating violence in visual media?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kerala High Court.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A division bench of the Kerala High Court (केरल उच्च न्यायालय) including Justice C S Sudha raised questions about how far the state can interfere in regulating violence in visual media.

• The observations came in the context of censorship and freedom of expression under Article 19 (अनुच्छेद 19).

• The Kerala High Court is located at Kochi (Ernakulam).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The Kerala High Court has jurisdiction over the state of Kerala and the Union Territory of Lakshadweep.

• Film certification in India is handled by the Central Board of Film Certification (CBFC).

NOTE

• Delhi High Court (Option 2): The High Court for the NCT of Delhi, located in New Delhi.

• Calcutta High Court (Option 3): The oldest High Court in India (est. 1862), with jurisdiction over West Bengal and Andaman & Nicobar Islands.

• Bombay High Court (Option 4): One of the oldest High Courts, with jurisdiction over Maharashtra, Goa and some UTs.

question: As the Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana (PMJDY) completed 10 years in August 2024, which ministry oversees its implementation?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Ministry of Finance.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana (प्रधानमंत्री जन धन योजना) is implemented by the Ministry of Finance through its Department of Financial Services.

• Launched on 28 August 2014, it is the world's largest financial inclusion scheme, providing zero-balance bank accounts.

• It completed 10 years in August 2024.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• PMJDY accounts come with a RuPay debit card, accident insurance cover and overdraft facility.

• The scheme is central to the JAM trinity (Jan Dhan–Aadhaar–Mobile) enabling Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT).

NOTE

• Ministry of Home Affairs (Option 2): Handles internal security, police and border management; not financial inclusion.

• Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers' Welfare (Option 3): Oversees farm schemes like PM-KISAN, not PMJDY.

• Ministry of Defence (Option 4): Manages the armed forces and national defence, unrelated to banking schemes.

question:
Which of the following is a report published by Reserve Bank of India?
I. Financial Stability Report
II. Handbook of Statistics on Indian Economy
solution_text:
The correct answer is Both I and II.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Both the Financial Stability Report and the Handbook of Statistics on Indian Economy are publications of the Reserve Bank of India (भारतीय रिज़र्व बैंक).

• The Financial Stability Report (FSR) is a half-yearly report assessing risks to financial stability.

• The Handbook of Statistics on Indian Economy is an annual statistical compendium of macro-economic and financial data.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Other key RBI publications include the Annual Report, Monetary Policy Report and the Report on Trend and Progress of Banking in India.

• The RBI was established on 1 April 1935 and nationalised in 1949.

NOTE

• Only I (Option 1): Incorrect, as the Handbook of Statistics is also an RBI publication.

• Only II (Option 2): Incorrect, as the Financial Stability Report is also published by the RBI.

• Neither I nor II (Option 4): Incorrect, since both reports are published by the RBI.

question: In _____, the All-India Kabaddi Federation came into existence
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1950.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The All-India Kabaddi Federation (अखिल भारतीय कबड्डी महासंघ) came into existence in 1950.

• It was formed to standardise the rules and promote Kabaddi (कबड्डी) across the country.

• Kabaddi is a traditional contact team sport of Indian origin.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The Amateur Kabaddi Federation of India (AKFI) was later founded in 1973.

• Kabaddi was included in the Asian Games as a demonstration sport in 1951 and became a medal event in 1990.

NOTE

• 1952 (Option 2): Not the year of formation of the All-India Kabaddi Federation.

• 1953 (Option 3): Incorrect year for this federation.

• 1954 (Option 4): Incorrect year; the federation was already formed by then.

question: 'Faster Than Lightning: My Story' is the autobiography of which of the following Olympian?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Usain Bolt.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• 'Faster Than Lightning: My Story' is the autobiography of Jamaican sprinter Usain Bolt (उसैन बोल्ट).

• He is regarded as the greatest sprinter of all time, holding world records in the 100m and 200m.

• He won multiple Olympic gold medals across the 2008, 2012 and 2016 Games.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• His world records are 9.58 seconds (100m) and 19.19 seconds (200m), both set in 2009.

• He was nicknamed 'Lightning Bolt' for his speed and signature celebration pose.

NOTE

• Carl Lewis (Option 1): An American track and field legend with nine Olympic golds; not the author of this book.

• Justin Gatlin (Option 3): An American sprinter and Bolt's rival, but not the author.

• Yohan Blake (Option 4): A Jamaican sprinter and Bolt's training partner; not the author.

question: In Dravida style of architecture, the front wall has an entrance gateway in its centre, which is known as a
solution_text:
The correct answer is Gopuram.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In Dravida (द्रविड़) style temple architecture, the ornate entrance gateway in the centre of the front wall is called a Gopuram (गोपुरम).

• Gopurams are typically tall, pyramidal tower-gateways richly decorated with sculptures.

• The Dravida style flourished in South India under dynasties like the Pallavas, Cholas and Nayakas.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• A Dravida temple is usually enclosed within a compound wall with the gopuram as the main entrance.

• The central shrine tower in the Dravida style is called the Vimana (unlike the Shikhara of the Nagara style).

NOTE

• Pada (Option 2): Refers to the base or foot/pillar segment in temple architecture, not the gateway.

• Prastara (Option 3): The entablature or horizontal superstructure above the pillars.

• Griva (Option 4): The neck-like part of the temple tower just below the crowning member (shikhara/stupi).

question: 'Nazu' festival is celebrated in which of the following state?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Nagaland.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Nazu festival is one of the most important festivals of the Pochury tribe of Nagaland (नगालैंड).

• It is celebrated for about ten days, typically in February, marking the agricultural cycle with dance and music.

• The Khupililie dance (खुपिलिली नृत्य) is performed during this festival.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Nagaland is famous for the Hornbill Festival, called the 'Festival of Festivals', held at Kisama.

• Other Naga festivals include Sekrenyi (Angami), Moatsu (Ao) and Tuluni (Sumi).

NOTE

• Assam (Option 1): Celebrates Bihu (Rongali, Bhogali, Kongali); Nazu is not an Assamese festival.

• West Bengal (Option 3): Known for Durga Puja and Poila Boishakh; not Nazu.

• Telangana (Option 4): Celebrates Bathukamma and Bonalu, not the Nazu festival.

question: 'Tlanglam' is a famous dance performed in which of the following Indian state/Union Territory?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Mizoram.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Tlanglam is a famous folk dance of Mizoram (मिज़ोरम), performed by the Mizo community.

• It is a group dance featuring rhythmic movements, usually accompanied by drums and gongs.

• Mizo dances are performed during festivals and community celebrations.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Other well-known Mizo dances include Cheraw (the bamboo dance), Khuallam and Chheihlam.

• Mizoram's major festivals include Chapchar Kut, Mim Kut and Pawl Kut.

NOTE

• Kerala (Option 2): Known for classical dances like Kathakali and Mohiniyattam, not Tlanglam.

• Himachal Pradesh (Option 3): Famous for Nati and Kayang folk dances.

• Jammu and Kashmir (Option 4): Known for Rouf, Dumhal and Kud dances.

question: What is a disadvantage of friction?
option_3: It prevents objects from wearing out
option_4: It causes wear and tear of materials
solution_text:
The correct answer is It causes wear and tear of materials.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A major disadvantage of friction (घर्षण) is that it causes wear and tear of surfaces and materials in contact.

• Friction also produces heat and reduces the efficiency of machines by wasting energy.

• It opposes relative motion between two surfaces in contact.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Friction is reduced using lubricants, ball bearings and by streamlining shapes.

• Despite disadvantages, friction is essential for walking, gripping and braking.

NOTE

• It increases speed (Option 1): Incorrect — friction opposes motion and generally reduces speed.

• It improves machinery efficiency (Option 2): Incorrect — friction lowers efficiency by wasting energy as heat.

• It prevents objects from wearing out (Option 3): Incorrect — friction actually causes objects to wear out.

question: The Parker Solar Probe, launched to study the Sun by moving in a solar orbit, is a mission of which space agency?
solution_text:
The correct answer is NASA.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Parker Solar Probe is a mission of NASA (नासा), the space agency of the United States.

• Launched in 2018, it is designed to fly through the Sun's outer atmosphere (corona) to study solar wind and heat.

• It is the first spacecraft named after a living person, physicist Eugene Parker.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The probe uses gravity assists from Venus to gradually approach the Sun.

• It has set records for the fastest human-made object and the closest approach to the Sun.

NOTE

• JAXA (Option 1): The Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency; not the operator of Parker Solar Probe.

• ISRO (Option 2): India's space agency, whose solar mission is Aditya-L1, not the Parker Solar Probe.

• CNES (Option 4): The French national space agency; not associated with this mission.

question: As of March 2025, under the National Supercomputing Mission (NSM) how many supercomputers have been deployed across India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 34.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• As of March 2025, a total of 34 supercomputers had been deployed across India under the National Supercomputing Mission (राष्ट्रीय सुपरकंप्यूटिंग मिशन).

• The NSM was launched in 2015 to build indigenous supercomputing capacity.

• It is jointly implemented by the Department of Science and Technology (DST) and MeitY, executed by C-DAC and IISc.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Supercomputers under NSM include the PARAM series such as PARAM Shivay, PARAM Siddhi-AI and PARAM Rudra.

• These systems support research in weather forecasting, drug discovery, AI and computational science.

NOTE

• 28 (Option 1): Not the figure reported as of March 2025.

• 40 (Option 3): An overstated figure for deployed supercomputers under NSM.

• 46 (Option 4): Incorrect; exceeds the actual number deployed.

question:
Which of the following statement regarding income is correct?
I. Out of private income, what finally reaches the households is known as personal income.
II. The total national income of the country is composed of two parts private income and public income.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Both I and II.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Statement I is correct: out of private income (निजी आय), the part that finally reaches households is known as personal income.

• Statement II is correct: the total national income (राष्ट्रीय आय) can be viewed as composed of private income and public income.

• Public income refers to income accruing to the public sector (government and public enterprises).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Personal income minus direct taxes gives disposable personal income.

• National income aggregates like GDP, GNP and NNP are core concepts in macroeconomics.

NOTE

• Only I (Option 1): Incorrect, because statement II is also correct.

• Only II (Option 2): Incorrect, because statement I is also correct.

• Neither I nor II (Option 4): Incorrect, since both statements are valid.

question: The National Logistics Policy in India was launched in _____.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 2022.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The National Logistics Policy (राष्ट्रीय लॉजिस्टिक्स नीति) was launched by the Government of India in September 2022.

• Its aim is to reduce logistics costs and improve the efficiency of the supply chain across the country.

• It complements the PM Gati Shakti (पीएम गति शक्ति) National Master Plan.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• The policy targets reducing India's logistics cost to be comparable with global benchmarks.

• It focuses on the IDEAS framework and the Unified Logistics Interface Platform (ULIP).

NOTE

• 2005 (Option 1): Incorrect; the policy did not exist then.

• 2010 (Option 2): Incorrect year for the National Logistics Policy.

• 2015 (Option 3): Incorrect; the policy was launched in 2022, not 2015.

question: What was the name of the principal minister in the Maratha kingdom?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Peshwa.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In the Maratha kingdom, the principal (prime) minister was called the Peshwa (पेशवा).

• The Peshwa headed the Ashta Pradhan (council of eight ministers) established by Chhatrapati Shivaji (छत्रपति शिवाजी).

• Later, the Peshwas of the Bhat family became the de facto rulers of the Maratha Empire from Pune.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Balaji Vishwanath was the first of the powerful hereditary Peshwas.

• Baji Rao I, a celebrated Peshwa, greatly expanded Maratha power.

NOTE

• Nawab (Option 1): A title for provincial governors/rulers under the Mughals, not the Maratha prime minister.

• Diwan (Option 3): The revenue/finance minister in Mughal and princely administration.

• Subedar (Option 4): A provincial governor of a Mughal suba (province).

question: Who among the following became the Nawab of Bengal after Alivardi Khan?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Sirajuddaulah.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Sirajuddaulah (सिराजुद्दौला) became the Nawab of Bengal in 1756 after the death of his grandfather Alivardi Khan.

• He fought the British East India Company in the Battle of Plassey (प्लासी का युद्ध) in 1757.

• He was defeated due to the betrayal of his commander Mir Jafar.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• The Battle of Plassey (1757) laid the foundation of British political power in India.

• Sirajuddaulah is also associated with the controversial 'Black Hole of Calcutta' episode.

NOTE

• Mir Jafar (Option 1): Became Nawab after Plassey (1757) with British support, not immediately after Alivardi Khan.

• Mir Qasim (Option 2): Succeeded Mir Jafar and later fought the British at the Battle of Buxar (1764).

• Murshid Quli Khan (Option 3): The founder of the independent Bengal Nawabi, who ruled much before Alivardi Khan.

question: About _____ per cent of the total road length in India are categorised as rural roads.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 80.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• About 80 per cent of the total road length (सड़क लंबाई) in India is categorised as rural roads (ग्रामीण सड़कें).

• Rural roads connect villages to markets, towns and the wider road network.

• The Pradhan Mantri Gram Sadak Yojana (PMGSY), launched in 2000, aims to provide all-weather rural road connectivity.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• India has one of the largest road networks in the world.

• Roads in India are classified as National Highways, State Highways, District roads, Rural roads and Border roads.

NOTE

• 60 (Option 2): An underestimate of the share of rural roads.

• 40 (Option 3): Incorrect; far lower than the actual proportion of rural roads.

• 20 (Option 4): Incorrect; a very small figure not matching the standard estimate.

question: Who was architect of Indian Planning?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Prasanta Chandra Mahalanobis.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Prasanta Chandra Mahalanobis (प्रशांतचंद्र महालनोबिस) is regarded as the architect of Indian planning.

• He designed the Second Five-Year Plan (1956–61) based on the Mahalanobis model emphasising heavy industry.

• He founded the Indian Statistical Institute (भारतीय सांख्यिकी संस्थान) in Kolkata.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• He introduced the statistical measure known as the Mahalanobis distance.

• 29 June is celebrated as National Statistics Day in India in his honour.

NOTE

• Sardar Vallabh Bhai Patel (Option 2): The 'Iron Man of India' and first Home Minister, who integrated the princely states.

• Manmohan Singh (Option 3): Economist and former PM associated with the 1991 economic reforms, not the architect of planning.

• Jay Prakash Narayan (Option 4): A freedom fighter and leader of the Total Revolution movement, not an economic planner.

question: There are broadly _____ sets of factors that influence migration.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 2.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• There are broadly two sets of factors that influence migration (प्रवासन) — push factors and pull factors.

• Push factors drive people away from a place (e.g., unemployment, poverty, disasters).

• Pull factors attract people to a new place (e.g., jobs, better facilities, security).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Migration can be internal (within a country) or international (across borders).

• In India, marriage and employment are among the major reasons for migration.

NOTE

• 3 (Option 2): Incorrect; migration is broadly explained by two sets of factors, not three.

• 4 (Option 3): Incorrect number of factor sets.

• 5 (Option 4): Incorrect; does not match the push-pull classification.

question: Rig Veda is a collection of approximately how many hymns?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1028.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Rig Veda (ऋग्वेद) is a collection of approximately 1028 hymns (सूक्त).

• These hymns are organised into 10 Mandalas (books).

• It is the oldest of the four Vedas and one of the oldest religious texts in the world.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The hymns are dedicated to deities such as Indra, Agni, Varuna and Soma.

• The Gayatri Mantra is found in the Rig Veda (Mandala 3), composed by sage Vishwamitra.

NOTE

• 508 (Option 1): Incorrect; understates the number of hymns in the Rig Veda.

• 838 (Option 2): Incorrect number of hymns.

• 1508 (Option 4): Incorrect; overstates the number of Rig Vedic hymns.
